अनुुपातत कोो 26.3% (2018) से बढ़ाकर 2035 ततक 50% करना है. हमें एनईपीी 2020 का हिससा बनना चाहिए और अन्य उचच शिक्षाक्षा संस्थाानों कोो उनके विकास, सामुुदायिक जुड़ााव और सेवा, अभ्यास के विभिनन क्षेत्रों में योगगदान, उचच शिक्षाक्षा प्रणाली के लिलिए संकायय विकास और स्कूल ी शिक्षाक्षा कोो समर्थन देने में सहायतता करनीी चाहिए. आईओई और हमारे रिकॉर्ड के साथ, मैं हैदराबाद विशवविद्यालयय कोो हमारे छात्रों की बेहततरी के लिलिए एनईपीी दवारा परिकल्पितत शिक्षण और अनुुसंधान प्रदान करने की क्पना करतता हूँ. मैं एनईपीी और आईओई अधिदेश दवारा प्रोतसाहितत अंततर्राष्ट्रीययकरण के माध्यम से बेहततर छात्र विविधतता की भीी और सेवाओं का लाभ उठठाकर इसे विशव स्तर पर सर्वश्ेष्ठ और उच्चततम श्ेणीी में शामिल कियया जा सकतता है. हमने संकायय सदस्यों के शोोध बुनिययादी ढाँचे में सुुधार के लिलिए रिसर्च कॉल जैसे कई कार्यक्रमों की घोोषणा की है. अब ततक 50 करोड़ रुपयये की 128 परियोोजनाएँ प्रदान की जा चुुकी हैं. नवीीनततम शोोध कॉल अजा/अजजा/ महिलाओं और दिव्यांगग व्यक्तिययों पर केंद्रितत है. शिक्षकों के लिलिए एक व्यावसायिक विकास निधि भीी शुुरू की गगई है. प्रारंभिक चरण में 3 शोोध अध्यक्ष प्रोफेसर भीी नियुुक्त किए गगए हैं. हाल ही में, पीीजीी कार्यक्रम में टॉपर्स के लिलिए स्टूडेंट अचीीवर्स अवार्ड, नॉन-नेट पीीएचडीडी फेलोशि प धारकों के लिलिए प्रकाशन-आधारितत प्रोतसाहन, भारतत के बाहर सम्मेलनों में भागग लेने के लिलिए सभीी हिततधारकों कोो प्रति व्यक्ति 1 लाख रुपयये की अंततर्राष्ट्रीयय ययात्रा सहायतता, कौशल विकास कार्यक्रम पेश करने, विज्ान विभाग जैव प्ौद्योगिकी एवं जैव सूचना विज्ान विभाग प्रणालीी एवं कम्प्यूयूटेशनल जीीव विज्ान विभाग प्रति वर्ष, संकाय कोो भारत और विदेशों से हमारीी प्रवेश अधिसूचनाओं के उत्तर में सबसे अधिक आवेदन प्ाप्त होते हैं. शैक्षणिक कार्यक्रमों, पात्रता मानदंडों और प्रवेश प्रक्रिया के साथ-साथ संकाय प्रोफाइल का विवरण संकाय के वेब पेज (http://sls.uohyd.ac.in) से प्ाप्त किया जा सकता है. संकाय ने अपनीी यात्ा पुराने विज्ान परिसर में स्थित एक साधारण परिसर से शुरू की थीी. अब यह 2,38,345 वर्ग फुट के प्लिंथ क्षेत्र वाले एक नए केंद्रीय रूप से वातानुकूलित भवन में परिवर्तित होो गया है. आधुनिक भवन में कुल 65 अनुसंधान प्रयोोगशालाएँ, कक्षााएँ, शिक्षण प्रयोोगशालाएँ, केंद्रीय उपकरण सुविधाएँ, कोशिका और सूक्ष्मजीीव संवर्धन सुविधाएँ, सेमिनार हॉल और सभागार हैं. मचछर प्रजनन सुविधा के साथ एक अतयाधुनिक पशु गृृह, और पूरीी तरह कार्यात्मक और तीीसरे पक्ष दवारा मूलयांकित जैव सुरक्षाा स्तर 3 (बीीएसएल-3) सुविधा, राजसीी जीीव विज्ान संकाय भवन में हाल हीी में जोोडे गए हैं. ये नए परिवर्धन और डीीबीीटीी-बूसट के अधीीन जैव प्ौद्योगिकी विभाग से विशवविदयालय अंतःविषय जीीवन विज्ान विभाग शिक्षाा और अनुसंधान कार्यक्रम (डीीबीीटीी-बिलडर) कार्यक्रम के लिए वित्त पोोषण वास्तव में संकायों के अंतःविषय अनुसंधान कोो बढावा देता है. जीीव विज्ान संकाय के संरक्षण में, कई छात्र विशव स्तर के वैज्ञानिक, अकादमिक नेता और उद्यमीी बन गए. संकाय की फैकल्टीी दवारा किए गए शोोध कार्य अकसर अंतरराष्ट्रीय खयाति प्ाप्त पत्रिकाओं में दिखाई देते हैं और विशव की सर्वश्ेष्ठ प्रतिभाओं का धयान आकर्षित करते हैं, जिसके परिणामसवरूप अंतर्राष्ट्रीय सहयोोग स्थापित हुआ है. अधिकांश प्रयोोगशालाओं ने अंतर्राष्ट्रीय अनुदान जीते हैं और अधिकांश ने प्रमुख देशों के साथ द्विपक्षीीय वैज्ञानिक सहयोोग में सफलतापूर्वक भाग लिया है. अपने शोोध योोगदान के लिए, संकाय ने भारतीीय विज्ान कांग्ेस एसोसिएशन (ISCA) दवारा स्थापित मिलेनियम पलैकस ऑफ ऑनर, सीीएसआईआर, नई दिल्लीी दवारा दिए गए शांति सवरूप भटनागर पुरसकार सहित कई मान्यताएँ जीतीी हैं. अच्छीी संखया में फैकल्टीी तीीनों प्रमुख विज्ान अकादमियों के फेलोो चुने गए हैं और जेसीी बोोस फेलोशिप; फुलब्ाइट इंटरनेशनल एजुकेशन एडमिनिस्ट्ेटर पुरसकार जैसे प्रतिष्ठित सम्ान जीते हैं. संकाय के अधिकांश विभाग यूजीीसीी- डीीआरएस/डीीएसटीी-एफआईएसटीी योोजनाओं दवारा वित्त पोषित हैं. जीीव विज्ान संकाय विशवविदयालय के अंतर्गत स्थापित उन कुछ संकायों में से एक है जोो डीीबीीटीी-बिलडर कार्यक्रम के अंतर्गत जैव प्ौद्योगिकी विभाग (डीीबीीटीी), नई दिल्लीी से अनुदान प्ाप्त करते हैं. इस शैक्षणिक वर्ष के दौरान, जीीव विज्ान संकाय कोो उद्योोग और सीीएसआईआर, डीीएसटीी, एसईआरबीी, डीीबीीटीी, एमओई और आईसीीएमआर जैसीी सरकारीी वित्त पोोषण एजेंसियों से लगभग 39 करोड़ रुपये का बाहय वित्त पोोषण प्ाप्त हुआ. इसके अलावा, देश में जीीव विज्ान संकाय के मासटर छात्ों ने यूजीीसीी- सीीएसआईआर-नेट परीक्षाा उत्तीर्ण करके प्रभावशालीी प्रदर्शन किया है. छात्ों का चयन प्रधानमंत्री अनुसंधान फैलोशिप के लिए भीी किया जाता है और कई विदेशीी छात्र नियमित रूप से जीीव विज्ान संकाय में शोोध इंटर्नशिप करते हैं. जीीव विज्ान संकाय ने विभिनन वित्त पोोषण एजेंसियों से प्ाप्त धन का प्रभावीी ढंग से उपयोोग कर अतयाधुनिक शिक्षण प्रयोोगशालाएँ, वास्तविक समय पीीसीीआर मशीीन, प्रतिदीप्तिि-सक्रिय सेल सॉर्टिंंग (एफएसीीएस) सुविधा, माइक्रोएरे सपॉटर/ विशलेषक और हाइब्रिडाइजेशन ओवन, अगलीी पीीढ़ीी की अनुक्रमण प्रणालीी, बायोोरुपटर, क्रॉस लिंकर, इलेक्ट्रोपोोरेटर, ल्यूमिनोमीीटर, नॅॅनोो-ड्ॉप मशीीन, एचपीीएलसीी, एफपीीएलसीी और एकेटीी पायलट, सीीडीी स्पेक्ट्रोफोोटोमीीटर, प्रतिदीप्तिि 57 50वाँ वार्षिक प्रतिवेदन स्पेक्ट्रोफोोटोमीीटर, सतह पलास्मोोन अनुनाद, रेडियोोधर्मीी सुविधा, प्रोटिओमिकस-एमएएलडीीआई/एमएस-एमएस/टीीओएफ- कयू केमिडोोक-इमेजिंग सिस्टम, रोोबोटिक क्रिसटलाइजेशन सिस्टम एलसीी-एमएस और जीीसीी-एमएस मेटाबोोलोमिक रिसर्च के लिए, इमेजिंग, ग्रीन हाउस सुविधा और बायोो-सेफ्टीी लेवल थ्री सुविधा (बीीएसएल3) बनाई है. हाल हीी में डीीबीीटीी-बिलडर के सहयोोग से, कई उपकरण खरीदे जा रहे हैं. मेटाबोोलिक फलकस एनालाइज़र, एनिमल हाउस के लिए बुनियादीी ढाँचा - एनेस्थीसिया मशीीन, क्षैैतिज आयताकार स्वचालित सटेरिलाइज़र, लैमिनार फ्लोो सिस्टम. इन केंद्रीय सुविधाओं के अलावा, संकाय कोो परिसर में स्थित नॅॅनोोटेक्नोोलॉजीी केंद्र, सेंट्रल इंस्ट्रूमेंटेशन लैबोोरेटरीी (सीीआईएल) और मॉडलिंग, सिमुलेशन और डिज़ाज़ाइन सेंटर (सीीएमएसडीी) में स्थापित बुनियादीी ढाँचागत सुविधाओं तक पहुँच प्ाप्त है, जिनमें ट्रांांसमिशन इलेक्ट्ॉन माइक्रोस्कोोप (टीीईएम), एटॉमिक फोर्स माइक्रोस्कोोप (एएफएम) और उच्च-स्तरीीय कम्प्यूयूटेशनल सुविधाएँ शामिल हैं. जीीव विज्ान संकाय कई संगोष्ठियों, सम्ेलनों और परिचर्चाओं का आयोोजन कर चुका है. संकाय ने विशव भर से कई प्रतिष्ठित संकाय सदसयों और प्रख्यात वैज्ञानिकों कोो आमंत्रित किया है. जीीवन विज्ान संकाय के डीीबीीटीी-बिलडर आउटरीच कार्यक्रम के अंतर्गत, 17 फ़रवरीी से 21 फ़रवरीी 2025 तक ‘Integrated approaches in understanding protein structure, dynamics, and interaction’ विषय पर एक कार्यशाला का आयोोजन किया जा रहा है. साइटिवा के साथ कार्यशाला – Training on SPR (Biacore) and protein purification system (Akta Pilot) – विषय पर प्रशिक्षण के लिए यह कार्यशाला दिनांक 19 फ़रवरीी से 21 फ़रवरीी, 2025 तक आयोोजित की जाएगीी . संकाय ने एक कौशल विकास केंद्र भीी स्थापित किया है जोो शोोधकर्ताओं और शोोध प्रशिक्षुुओं कोो उनके चुने हुए विषय क्षेेत्ों में प्रशिक्षण प्रदान करता है. शैक्षणिक वर्ष 2024-2025 के दौरान ये प्रशिक्षण कार्यक्रम आयोोजित किए गए: ग्रीष्मकालीीन अनुसंधान इंटर्नशिप कार्यक्रम; विज्ान अकादमियों का ग्रीष्मकालीीन सकूल; छात्र प्रेक्षण; फ्लोो साइटोमेट्री पर शरदकालीीन सकूल; बायोोई3 परिचर्चा; पशु कोशिका संवर्धन और औषधि खोोज पर कार्यशाला; प्रोटीीन संरचना, गतिकी और अंतःक्रियाओं पर कार्यशाला; CRISPR-Cas9 प्ौद्योगिकी पर कार्यशाला; जीीव विज्ान में सांख्यिकीय अनुप्रयोोग; स्नातकोोत्तर छात्ों के लिए इंटर्नशिप. इन गहन शैक्षणिक गतिविधियों और उत्कृृषट बुनियादीी ढाँचे के कारण, जीीव विज्ान संकाय कोो 'छात्ों की आकांक्षाा और विदवानों का गंतवय' के रूप में जाना जाता है. प्रो. आनंद के. कोंडापि, जैव प्ौद्योगिकी और जैव सूचना विज्ान विभाग, जीीव विज्ान संकाय के संकाय- अध्यक्ष हैं (उनके प्रोफाइल कोो http://sls.uohyd.ac.in/ पर देखा जा सकता है) 4.4.1 Statement showing the number of students on 62 rolls Course/Subject/Category and gender wise vi From the Vice-Chancellor’s Desk I'm delighted to present the University of Hyderabad's annual report, highlighting our remarkable progress in education and research. As we complete four successful years of the Institution of Eminence (IoE) project, we're poised to reach new heights. Global Recognition Our university's consistent focus on quality research and teaching has earned us a spot in the QS Rankings 2026, with a ranking of 801-850 globally. We're among the top universities worldwide and ranked 18th among Indian universities in the National Institutional Ranking Framework (NIRF) 2025. Our research publications have secured us the top spot among multidisciplinary Indian universities in the Nature Index 2025 ranking. Student Strength and Diversity This year, our student strength stands at 5,750, with 30.5% research scholars pursuing Ph.D. and M.Tech programs. Women students comprise 46.2% of the total strength, while 27.5% of students belong to reserved Basuthkar Jagadeeshwar Rao Vice-Chancellor, University of Hyderabad vii Prof. C. R. Rao Road, Gachibowli Central University P.O. Hyderabad – 500 046. categories (SC/ST/PH) and 37.5% from OBC categories. We've also seen a significant increase in international students, with 250 students enrolled in various programs. The University of Hyderabad has successfully uploaded a total of 44800 records of the Degrees awarded to the Digilocker NAD. All Degrees awarded from 1977 to 2024 have been uploaded. Our university is now part of the Ministry’s CUET for the admissions. I am happy to inform you all that the University has received close to 30,999 applications for all courses other than PhD. Research Excellence Our faculty, numbering over 400, produced more than 562 research publications including 70 books, during the year. Our faculty have been associated with several important national and international bodies, held Professorships of distinction, both in India and abroad, and participated in the global educational arena with as much vigour as we have always done. Furthermore, they have been funded quite handsomely receiving grants from national and international funding agencies like UGC, MHRD, DBT, DST, EU, DoE, IUSSTF and so on. The University’s current extramural R&D funding is about Rs. 350 crores. Our long-term vision and mission is “National Needs, Global Standards”. Our core values seek innovation and interdisciplinary, integrating hard sciences with humanistic studies and social inquiry, reinvigorating literary and linguistic studies with digital technology. University’s research work aspires to global standards in order to truly fulfil national needs. I am delighted to record here a recent study by Stanford and published in the highly respected journal PLOS Biology shows 29 of our faculty/researchers figure in the list of top researchers. Institution of Eminence Initiatives The University of Hyderabad's Institution of Eminence (IoE) status is a huge recognition of its standing and potential to join the world's best institutions. To leverage this, the university has announced several initiatives, including research calls to boost faculty research infrastructure, with 128 projects worth ₹50 crores already awarded. The latest research call focuses on SC/ST/Women and persons with disability. The university is also working on internationalization through the IoE Chair Professor and International Fellows scheme, and enhancing industry involvement through public-private partnerships and research clusters. New infrastructure developments are Inter-disciplinary centre; HRDC building; International guest house; Administrative building and Hostels for boys and girls. NEP 2020 and IoE Initiatives We're committed to implementing the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020, focusing on interdisciplinary research, innovation, and community engagement. Under the IoE project, we've launched new programs, viii ix including research calls, professional development funds for teachers, and student achiever awards. We've also initiated internationalization efforts, including the IoE Chair Professor and International Fellows scheme. Infrastructure Development We're expanding our infrastructure with new buildings, including an interdisciplinary center, HRDC building, international guest house, and hostels. These developments will enhance our research and teaching capabilities. Looking Ahead As we strive to become a global leader in higher education, our vision of "National Needs, Global Standards" aligns with the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). I congratulate our faculty, students, and staff for their tireless efforts and dedication to excellence. I look forward to even greater achievements for the University of Hyderabad. Department of Systems & Computational Biology About the School Established in 1977, The School of Life Sciences has witnessed phenomenal progress and established itself as one of the largest and most vibrant Schools in the University system in the country. With an emphasis on interdisciplinary teaching and research, the school produces finest graduates in modern biology, biotechnology, bioinformatics and systems biology. The performance of its alumni, students together with the contributions of the faculty, placed University at highest rank in research output in the recent Nature Index rankings. The School consists of five Departments: Department of Biochemistry Department of Plant Sciences Department of Animal Biology Department of Biotechnology & Bioinformatics Department of Systems & Computational Biology Every year, the School receives highest number of applications in response to our admission notifications both from India and abroad. Details of academic programmes, eligibility criteria and admission process along with faculty profile can be accessed from the web page of the school (http://sls.uohyd.ac.in). The School started its journey from a modest premises located at the old science complex. It has moved out to a new centrally air-conditioned building with a plinth area of 2,38,345 sft. The modern building is designed for housing a total of 65 research laboratories, class-rooms, teaching laboratories, central instrumentation facilities, cell and microbial culture facilities, seminar hall and auditorium. A state of the art animal house with mosquito breeding facility, and a fully functional and third party evaluated Biosafety Level 3 (BSL-3) facility are the recent additions to majestic School of Life Sciences building. These new additions and funding from Department of Biotechnology under DBT-Boost to University Interdisciplinary Life Science Departments for Education and Research programme (DBT-BUILDER)programme is indeed a boost to the Schools interdisciplinary research. The well-equipped laboratories, committed, trained faculty together with highly talented and motivated students contribute for establishing an excellent academic ecosystem at SLS. Under the tutelage of SLS faculty, a number of students transformed into World Class Scientists, academic leaders and entrepreneurs. Research work done by the faculty of the school frequently appear in journals of international reputes and attracted the attention of world’s best talent. resulting in establishing international collaborations. Most of the labs have won international grants and successfully participated in bilateral scientific collaborations with most of the leading nations. In recognition of their research contributions, the faculty won a number of recognitions including Millennium Plaques of Honour instituted by Indian Science Congress Association (ISCA), Shanthi Swaroop Bhatnagar Prize, given by CSIR, New Delhi. A good number of faculty are elected fellows of all three leading science academies and won coveted recognitions like JC Bose fellowships, Fulbright International Education Administrators Awards. The vision of the faculty together with hard work of the committed students, helped SLS to win institutional grants from national and international agencies. The SLS won prestigious CAS (Center for Advanced Studies) grant from University Grants Commission (UGC), New Delhi. Most of the departments of the school are funded either by UGC-DRS / by DST-FIST schemes. The SLS is one of the few Schools under University set up to receive grants from Department of Biotechnology (DBT), New Delhi under DBT-BUILDER programme. During this academic year, SLS obtained about 39 crores approximately extramural funding from both industry and Govt. funding agencies like, CSIR, DST, SERB, DBT, MoE and ICMR. A rigorous selection process, based on the assessment of their research writing samples by the screening committee and their reasons for enrolling in the workshop training programme, led to the selection of around 20 PhD scholars (15 from the History Department and five from Folk Culture Studies) in their third and fourth years and thesis write-up stages for these workshop sessions. In the initial phase of the three-day workshop designed for PhD scholars in Folk Culture and History, three distinguished academics with expertise in academic writing for doctoral students and the publishing industry were invited. The three resource persons who offered their insights during the three days in October were Prof. K. Satyanarayana, Professor, Department of Cultural Studies, The English and Foreign Languages University (EFLU), Hyderabad), Dr. Prasun Chatterjee Deputy Head, Primus Books, Delhi, and Dr. Hashik NK Assistant Professor, Department of Cultural Studies, Tezpur University, Assam. The three-day workshops, led by subject matter experts, were not just lecture sessions, but interactive experiences designed to engage PhD scholars. The PhD candidates specialising in Folk Culture Studies presented their ongoing research in the first phase, receiving valuable critical feedback from the resource persons who acted as evaluators during the workshop. The event primarily focused on interactive sessions, offering tips for enhancing the quality of doctoral dissertations, developing theoretical frameworks and methodologies, and ensuring that each PhD candidate contributes effectively to original research. Noteworthy sessions from the workshop included “Critical Thinking and Writing”, “Writing a Research Paper or Doctoral Thesis Chapter”, and “Transforming a Thesis into a Book Manuscript.” The second and third workshops were held on the 21st and 22nd November and 12th and 13th December, 2024. The coordinators were Professors Anindita Mukhopadhyay and Eswara Rao respectively. Due to a sudden bereavement in the family Prof. Rao could not be present during the workshop and the activities were conducted by the Head of the department. In the second phase the experts were Prof.J.Devika, Centre for Development Studies, Thiruvananthapuram and Dr Pratyay Nath, Department of History, Ashoka University, Sonepat. Prof. Devika spoke on “Crafting a History of the Present of the Malayali Family: Some Thoughts” and “Towards an Intersectional Method in Writing the Histories of Subaltern Places”. Dr Pratyay Nath talked about “Methodological issues of Reading Imperial Sources against the Grain”, and “Akbar’s Pilgrimages to Ajmer and the Formation of the Mughal Empire”. He demonstrated how visual sources can be used as explanatory tools for writing history. For the third workshop our experts were Prof. Projit Behari Mukharji, Department of History, Ashoka University and Dr Meera Visvanathan, Department of Department of History, Shiv Nadar University. Projit B.Mukharji spoke on “Molecularizing Tribes: Genetics as Prosaic Science in Early Postcolonial India” and also introduced the methodology of practising History of Science, Technology and Medicine. Meera Visvanathan who is a practitioner of early Indian history, spoke on the “Complex Chronologies and Longue Durée Histories: New Narratives for Studying India’s Past” and discussed about the way a source like Land grants should be used for reconstruction of the past economic and social history. All the experts meticulously checked chapters written by the students related to their expertise and their critical comments were extremely useful. The students also presented their chapters and, in this domain, too, the experts suggested improvement which would allow them to curate their presentations in a succinct manner. The students feel that thy have hugely benefitted from the workshop, interactive sessions in particular, and the comments of the experts provided a direction to their work. The academic writing workshop emphasized the crucial skills necessary for PhD scholars aiming to become accomplished academic authors and researchers, both nationally and internationally. The resource persons and the workshop coordinator stressed the urgent necessity for PhD candidates to complete their dissertations and publish at least one peer-reviewed journal article in SCOPUS-listed journals before their PhD Viva and the awarding of their doctoral degree. The experts also emphasized on the habit of reading beyond their own research area. The workshop, in addition to offering these essential sessions, also outlined a roadmap for approaching the PhD journey as an exciting adventure filled with intellectual curiosity rather than experiencing monotony and boredom. In May 1985, the Academic Council decided that the Centre of Regional Studies would continue under the School of Social Sciences to facilitate interdisciplinary teaching and research in the field of Regional Studies, as initially recommended by the Fifth Five Year Plan Visiting Committee (AC on 15 May 1985 and EC on 13 June 1985). Established in 1985 according to the University Statutes and Ordinances, the Centre for Regional Studies (CRS) is the oldest Centre in the School of Social Sciences and the University itself. It commenced admissions for M.Phil. and Ph.D. programs from the academic year 1988-89 onwards. Since then, the Centre has awarded a total of 67 Ph.D. and 80 M.Phil. degrees from 1989-1990 to June 2024. The delineation of ‘regions’ serves as a significant framework for comprehending societal dynamics. The Centre for Regional Studies (CRS) operates as an interdisciplinary hub within the School of Social Sciences, with its focal point being the region as the unit of analysis. These regions can be further disaggregated into sub-regions, enabling a focused examination of specific themes or idiosyncrasies. These themes encompass urbanisation, industrialisation, identity conflicts, marginalised regions and groups, political intricacies, cultural underpinnings, and environmental implications. All disciplines within the realm of social sciences play pivotal roles in both the conceptualisation and implementation of this framework. CRS offers students the opportunity to engage with a regional approach to the study of socio-spatial transformations and to weave together concepts from various disciplines within the social sciences. The Centre’s educational program for students adopts a spatial perspective, providing a comprehensive understanding of complex social phenomena in their multidimensionality. The Centre for Folk Culture Studies is the first of its kind in the Central University system in India. It was established with the assistance of the Ford Foundation, USA. The Centre’s interdisciplinary and multi-perspectival approaches emphasis research and teaching in Folk Culture Studies in the milieu of contemporary ethnographic fieldwork. The Centre’s thrust is on the study of various aspects of folk expressive behaviour as a dialogue between human groups and their physical and social environments. The manifold folk forms are information banks and communication systems explicating the dynamics of adaptive processes in time and space. To decode and explain the folk expressive forms, the Centre is adopting a research strategy that combines the methodological procedures and theoretical approaches of both humanities and social sciences. At present, SEST offers M.Tech programmes in Materials Engineering, Nanoscience and Technology and Manufacturing Science and Engineering and Ph.D. programmes in Materials Engineering and Nanoscience and Technology and intends to offer Ph.D. programme in Manufacturing Science and Engineering soon. The school will be starting an integrated 5-year B.Tech & M.Tech program in Materials engineering from the academic year 2024. With this addition, the school will seamlessly cater to engineering 135 50TH ANNUAL REPORT education from the bachelor’s level to doctoral level. Furthermore, the school plans to offer new programs in emerging areas of engineering and specialized programs for working professionals. The school has moved into a dedicated facility for engineering that houses several state-of-the-art laboratories under a single roof, which provides an ideal environment to pursue cross-disciplinary research in engineering sciences and technology and to effectively collaborate with other schools in the university campus. SEST also collaborates with premier research institutions located in and around Hyderabad (namely DMRL, IICT, ARCI, NFC, NFTDC, NMDC and RCI), most of which are also formally recognized as school’s external research centers, which provide ample opportunities for the students to work on industry relevant projects. The school is also actively involved in international collaborative projects that provide students with exciting new opportunities abroad. The school has already been recognized for its excellence by the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India, with funding to the tune of Rs. 240 Lakhs under its FIST programme. The school, since its inception, has been able to attract research grants of more than Rs. 1946 lakhs from various external funding agencies and through other revenue generation modes. Atomic lasers, molecular computers, drug-receptor interactions, industrial catalysts, lubricants, and industrially important materials form part of this continuum and an understanding of this evolution needs all the three components of research, viz. theory, experiment and computation. Computer-based simulations now form an integral part of modern research methodology and in this era of science-driven-engineering and directed basic research, the role of scientific research, based on modelling, simulation and design, is of paramount importance. The primary requisite in using the third avenue of research for solving complex problems is a working, state-of-the- art High Performance Computing Facility (HPCF) Centre. The University of Hyderabad, having expertise in many of the above areas, fully appreciates the inter-dependence of Science, Engineering and Technology, and launched a uniquely conceived new programme of higher education and research. This initiative was launched through an imaginative programme of the UGC (recognizing the University for its Potential for excellence) by establishing a designated Centre for such activity (Centre for Modelling Simulation and Design – CMSD). This programme has been receiving generous support from DST under its FIST program. CMSD aims to nurture cross-disciplinary bridges, which are effective in generating new knowledge and creative explorations. The human resources generated from such efforts will be invaluable. Training individuals and organizations in specific hardware and software, undertaking of consultancy and turnkey projects, help convert real life phenomena into appropriate mathematical and computational models etc., are some of the important tasks that CMSD has embarked on. This Centre became operational from its new premises in December 2004. One of the unique academic features of this Centre is that all the active computational scientists working in widely different academic disciplines in the University Campus are Associate Faculty of the CMSD, and contribute their 143 50TH ANNUAL REPORT expertise and experience in furthering its academic objectives. Some of the research interests of these Members include: Physics of low dimensional systems, Topological defects in fluids in restricted geometries, Critical phenomena in complex fluids and magnetic systems, Monte Carlo simulations and development of novel sampling techniques, Genomics and bioinformatics, Protein folding, Cognitive neuroscience, Computational intelligence, Natural language understanding, Very Large Scale Integration (VLSI), Quantum Chemistry and Density Functional Theory, Molecular Modelling, Drug Design and Delivery, Design of new materials, weather forecastingetc. Short term courses have been so far conducted in the areas of Parallel Computing, Monte Carlo Simulation and Molecular Modelling etc. CMSD has been involved, over the past few years, in promoting and fostering multidisciplinary research programmes in Advanced Computational Methods, with focus on the core areas of Physics, Chemistry, Biology, Engineering Sciences and Computer Sciences, besides interest in related research areas like Finite Element Analysis as applied to Nanotechnology, Computational Fluid Dynamics, Ocean-atmosphere-climate Modelling, High-End-Visualization/ Virtual Reality, Modelling and Simulation of large/complex Systems, etc. Following are the facilities available at the Centre: 1) Data Centre: The Data Centre houses a HPC cluster with following configuration. a. The Library was established in 1975 and shifted to the present building in 1988. It was inaugurated by His Excellency Dr. Shankar Dayal Sharma, the then Vice-President of India, and named after Late Prime Minister Indira Gandhi. All the in-house Library Operations are fully computerized, including the Web OPAC, using the international Library Management Software Virtua supplied by VTLS Inc., USA. The Library automation activities have been moved to the CLOUD base using AWS since 2018. The UGC-INFLIBNET has identified the Library as one of the 26 document delivery centers in India for providing photocopies of journal articles to the research scholars of other Universities. Since 1990, the Library has achieved several distinctions in the country: a) The IGM Library is the first University Library to computerize all in-house operations. b) The first Library to computerize other Libraries (B.R. Ambedkar Open University, Telangana, and State Central Library, Hyderabad, Telangana.) c) The first University Library to start the PGDLAN Course under Distance Education mode since 1998 d) The first University Library to subscribe to Electronic e-journals and databases. e) The National Board of Higher Mathematics (NBHM) has identified this Library as a Regional Library for the Southern Region. f) The first University Library to establish a Centre of competency in digital libraries and e-learning with the assistance of SUN Microsystems and UGC. g) The first University Library to install a 3M Security Gate to avoid book thefts. h) The first University Library to become a governing member of OCLC, USA. i) The first University Library to install a 100 KVA solar power system The Library is kept open 24x7 throughout the year except for Five National holidays in a year. 8.1.1. Technical Specifications for High-Resolution and High-Speed Laser Scanning Confocal Microscope A Inverted Fluorescent Laser Scanning confocal Microscope with Live Cell Capability, with at least three laser lines, along with a super-resolution module for high-resolution imaging applications Bids are invited for a state-of-the-art imaging platform consisting confocal “Inverted fluorescent microscope with live cell imaging system, with at least three laser lines and a high-resolution module for a wide range of applications in life sciences and interdisciplinary sciences. OEM/authorized representatives can bid for any one/single part of the imaging platform. However, preference will be given to OEMs/their authorized representatives that can offer an integrated, robust imaging platform that can be upgradable to applications like, spinning disk, FRET, FRAP, FLIM and 2-camera system etc,. to fit into evolving research questions in the future. Sealed bids should reach the Tammineni lab, Room F8, School of Life Sciences, University of Hyderabad, Hyderabad on or before 04th Dec 2025 (Date) 5:30pm (time). Part A: A confocal ‘Inverted Fluorescent Microscope with Live Cell Capability Sl No Part A: Specification 1 Microscope: Fully Motorized Inverted Fluorescence Microscope for BF/Fluorescence with a dedicated remote touch panel/tab/controller and remote focus knob for controlling motorized components of the microscope. The system should be equipped with a built in Infinity port/stratum structure or double deck system for future laser introduction or FRAP upgradation/optical tweezer upgradation etc. The system should have proper drainage system to avoid any leakage from the dish into the precious optics. 2 Widefield tilting Binocular observation head with paired 10X eye pieces with dioptre adjustment. Bright LED light source for BF, DIC imaging applications controlled by imaging software and touch screen panel. 3 Programmable motorized X-Y scanning stage including sample holders for slides, 35/60 mm Petri dish, Labtech chambers and multi well dishes with multipoint, tile and mosaic imaging software (capable of fast 6D imaging). 4 Hardware & IR laser/LED (> 790 nm) Based Focus Drift compensation for long term live cell imaging application is mandatory and must be capable of working with plastic and cover glass bottom dishes. The drift compensator should be controlled by the remote touch screen panel with one touch autofocus to instantly focus the specimen mounted on plastic and glass bottom dishes. 5 Bright long working life LED Light Source with direct coupling for Fluorescence imaging, catering to the DAPI, CFP, YFP, FITC/GFP, RFP, mCherry, Cy3 and Cy5 fluorophores to be included. The light source should facilitate in capturing fast events with microsecond switching via TTL inputs via remote triggering (TTL, microsecond), Individual channel triggering (TTL, microsecond) for on/off control of selected channels. Triggering speed <20 μs at full power. A suitable TTL controller board/card should be supplied controlled by imaging software for fast switching of LED lines. 6 Narrow Band pass fluorescent filters cubes should include for DAPI, FITC/GFP, RFP/ mCherry Cy3 and Cy5 observation and imaging. 7 Motorized 6-position nosepiece with slots for DIC, Motorized Condenser with NA 0.55 or better with optical modules for DIC for respective objectives with built in transmitted shutter. 8 Minimum 8 position or higher motorized filter cube turret with built in motorized shutter for accommodating minimum 7 position fluorescent filters for sample visualization and camera-based imaging and one for BF/DIC Imaging 9 High precision Z-focus drive with step size of 10 nm or better. 10 Objectives: Plan super apochromat objectives - 40x/1.4 or better oil, 60/63x/1.42 oil immersion or better, 100X/1.45 oil or better, and confocal compatible lenses for 10X/0.40, Long Distance 20X/0.40 (WD 7.8 mm or better). DIC attachment for 20X, 40X, 60X and 100X should be the part of standard supply. All will be considered) the objectives should be plan Apo chromatically corrected. All the plan apochromatic objectives should have chromatic correction from 400-1000 nm both laterally and axially (<200nm axial between DAPI and Cy5) for precise colocalization studies in XYZ. (Please provide necessary data on website / brochure) The plan Apochromatic objectives should have uniform field of view (FOV) throughout wide FOV of large Chip SCMOS (>21mm). Low Fluorescence Immersion Oil 100ml should be provided (minimum 5 bottles). 11 Stage top CO2 incubator setup for long-term live cell imaging including incubation system with Temperature, CO2 and humidity control. The parameters for incubation system should be controlled by software with the ability to record the temperature, CO2 levels at peridics intervals of atleast 10 minutes . Temp collar/Objective heater for High NA objectives should be provided. 12 Specifications: Lasers All lasers should be the latest solid-state lasers with following laser wavelengths and powers. a. 477/488 nm: 100 mW or better b. 555/561 nm, 100 mW or better c. 638/640 nm: 100 mW or better All the Lasers should be stable solid-state laser controlled by Direct Modulation/AOTF for precise switching and swift selection of the desired laser lines. Mention the names of manufacturers of Lasers. The Laser Combiner should be from the microscope company itself for better integration and post- sale support. The laser combiner should onsite be upgradable to additional lasers such as 405, 445, 514 and 594nm. All lasers should be combined with high transmission beam splitters and delivered to the confocal scan head through high transmission efficiency optical fiber. The laser control should be through direct Modulation by high speed break out box for ultra-fast ON/OFF control and intensity modulation with individual laser lines, continuously variable (0 % - 100 %, 1 % increments). The breakout box should also be capable of controlling other third-party hardware such as perfusion system, electrophysiology, laser/ LED pulse pickers for advanced image acquisitions. Should be able to synchronize image camera with the image acquisition through TTL trigger for faster image acquisition. High Speed Super Resolution module: The super resolution module should be two-step image reconstruction based on High-Speed pattern illumination/high speed structured illumination module with automated optimization for different wavelengths & magnifications/multipoint spinning disc grid pattern. It should be based on low frequency suppression/filtering and high frequency pattern collection to generate high resolution images of 100-120nm in real time with at least 50FPS with full resolution. The image processing for high frequency patten filtering and high-resolution image construction should be online and real time. In the second step the system should have capability to further improve the lateral resolution through image restoration algorithms such as iterative deconvolution algorithm based a dedicated PSF fitting 3D deconvolution module with a dedicated algorithm to fit the Super Res PSF. The system should be able to generate high speed real time super resolution of both monolayer/2D samples and multilayer cell/tissues/spheroids 3D samples (cleared and uncleared specimens). The frame rate of the super resolution should be 100 FPS or better in full resolution and full FOV of the sCMOS camera with at least 2Kx2K resolution. Note: The super resolution image should be hardware based through optical theory. Provide white papers/patents/published research article on the techniques used. All the objectives including the 100X and objective should be compatible with Super resolution mode to achieve the highest spatial resolution of upto 100-120nm with high NA objectives. Detection: Detection units should be based on high QE Scientific CMOS Camera (Peak QE @560 nm >90%), resolution of 2Kx2K, pixel Size 6.5 micron X 6.5-micron, effective area of 13x 13 mm, Frame rate of up to 100FPS with full resolution and full FOV with Cam Link/Coax cable connection, Dark Current of < 0.06e/p/s and read noise <0.8 with slow scan (30FPS) and <1.0 with high speed scan (100FPS), dynamic range of 35,000:1, full well capacity of 30,000, The camera must be Peltier cooled (-10 Deg absolute) with active air cooling. The camera should have inlet outlet jacket for water cooling. The system should be upgradable to perform two colour simultaneous imaging capabilities in super resolution mode as well with > 1Kx1K and at least 100 FPS with an appropriate beam splitter. The image software should have multi camera control capabilities with an option to trigger the camera, perfusion pumps and other peripherals if required through TTL. Emission Filter Wheel: The system should be equipped with an integrated high speed (40 ms or better with adjacent positions), 10 positions fast filter wheel (2 nos). The filter wheels should be equipped with single band pass emission filters for DAPI, CFP, FITC, YFP, TRITC, mCherry, Cy3 and Cy5. All laser lines for confocal Imaging should be useable for imaging in the super resolution mode, GFP/mCherry should be offered for two color fast sequential imaging. Suitable Primary DMs (405/488/561/640) in the scan head should be offered. Quote for dual band pass (GFP/RFP/mCherry) emission filter for faster two- color excitation sequential imaging. 4. System control and Imaging Software: 1 Software should be capable of controlling every component of the system including microscope, confocal setup. The system should be able to switch seamlessly between confocal and super resolution mode using the software. It should be compatible for 3D, 4D, 5D and 6D imaging (X,Y,Z,t, multi colour, multi point). Image stitching in co-ordination with XYZ stage with dedicated Software module. The system software should have intuitive modules for multidimensional imaging such as experiment manager / jobs / sequence manager. The software should be capable of performing interactive Quantitative data analysis. 2 Advanced 3D image reconstruction with rendering from a Z- stack image series including 3D deconvolution capability in widefield, confocal and Super resolution deconvolution modalities (for all the PSFs such as widefield, Bright Field, point scanning confocal and spinning disc confocal and super resolution. The deconvolution modules should support importing the raw data from other image formats and perform auto-calibration to render high resolution images. It should be able pick up all the optical and wavelength parameters from the meta data and generate hypothetical PSF for 3 D and 2 D deconvolution. It should also be able to import actual PSF data generated from the sub resolution beads and perform realistic deconvolution. 3 Co-localization and histogram analysis with inbuild Parameters. 5 Hardware control: All the motorized components of the hardware including XY stage for multi-point and mosaic imaging, hardware based autofocus module, Emission filter wheels for fast sequential imaging, BF- LED light source for intensity and fast shutter control for multi-channel imaging, third party SCMOS cameras for high speed ratio imaging, third party TTL/triggered device control, DAQ card control for external light sources/lasers and perfusion systems, on stage CO2 incubator and other upgradable hardware modules such as TIRF, FRAP, confocal and super resolution systems. 6 Image Acquisition Modules: Simultaneous Dual / Triple / Quad Camera acquisition module for multipoint, multidimensional (XYZtʎ) 6D imaging & experimental preview. (multi point, stitching module to be offered with XY motorised stage) Over lay of imaging, Mark and find for multipoint and mosaic imaging, Realtime stitching of large samples with higher magnification, Multipoint and multi position imaging with hardware based autofocus. Online/real-time deconvolution. Modules to perform design and execute complicated experiments through drag and drop functions (Graphical experimental manager/Jobs/journals/experiment designer etc.) High Dynamic Range Imaging, Instant Extended focal imaging, simultaneous imaging of two channels with image splitters and multiple cameras, real time/instant EDF. A Real-Time controller: The controller should provide parallel command execution for motorized components such as LED/Laser switching, shuttering, swift movement of filter wheel and Z movement during fast two color XYZ time lapse imaging. The devise should support fast two color near simultaneous imaging using single camera with perfect over lapping of two colors. The process of closing the shutter and moving the filter wheels & Z steps should begin as soon as camera acquisition is done, during camera chip readout to avoid bleaching. Both filter wheel and laser/LED should switch/move in parallel to save time during two color imaging using single camera for perfect overlapping two colors during fast time lapse imaging (for vesicle tracking experiments). 7 Image Analysis: Multidimensional intensity measurement and data export to EXCEL format for further statistical analysis. Colocalization analysis with scatter plot display and statistical analysis, FRET and FRAP analysis, spatiotemporal measurement modules. 3D/volume rendering orthogonal slice view of 3D stacks. Calcium/Physiology/Ratio analysis module, background subtraction/correction, bleaching correction, cell count and confluency measurements, Object Classifier/ automated count and measure etc. The imaging software should be able to image large tissues/organoids/spheroids with lower magnifications and automatically detect them switch over to higher magnifications and acquire images and stitch to generate high resolution images. The system software should have integrated Deconvolution module (2D Real Time/2D/3D), and Artificial Intelligence based object classifier/segmentation and counting module. The imaging software should have an automated object detection based on automated, and AI based object detection with trained neural Network. The imaging software should have an automated object tracking of moving objects and analysis module with an ability to measure distance travelled with velocity of each manually or automatically selected objects. Software Package to automatically analyze moving objects which can divide over time, create a tree representation for the split tracks and get the quantitative information from their image data and export data into a data sheet and EXCEL for further analysis. 5. Technical Specifications A digital image correlation system The proposed 3D Digital Image Correlation (DIC) System should be a state-of-the-art, non-contact optical measurement solution for full-field strain and displacement mapping, which can operate at room temperature and high temperatures. The system should be designed to operate in compliance with ASTM standards for strain measurement, ensuring accuracy, reproducibility, and traceability of experimental data across a broad range of materials, including metallic alloys, ceramics, polymers, and composites etc. At room temperature as well as under elevated temperature conditions, the system will enable high- fidelity strain field measurements, supporting both quasi-static and dynamic mechanical testing. The optical configuration, calibration procedure, and software algorithms ensure compatibility with existing infrastructure while maintaining measurement precision across varied test environments. Importantly, the system shall be fully compatible with the existing Instron 5982 Universal Testing Machine and Zwick Vibrophore 100, thereby enabling direct integration for monotonic, cyclic, and fatigue testing applications. The architecture should be modular and upgradable, permitting future enhancements. This purchase will establish a versatile, scalable, and future-ready experimental platform for advanced materials characterization, supporting both ongoing research and future demands in structural and functional material development. Complete package with the following features:- 1. Image Capture:- Manual, Time, Streaming, Images in block as per frame rate, variable time capture and Analog Capture. 2. Indication in color code if the image is focused and the noise levels. 6 3. Indication in color code if the image is uniformly illuminated. 4. Capture of external analog signals with the images – synchronization with the UTM. 5. Parameters to be Measured. a) Displacements - X, Y & Z Directions. b) Strains: éxx , éyy , éxy , Principal, Von Mises and Tresca strains. Resolution of Strain Measurement – 25 μm or better. c) Velocity Computation. d) In Plane rotations. e) Full Field Stress Computations. f) Poisson’s Ratio. g) User Defined Variables. 6) Strain Computation Algorithms:- Lagrange , Hencky, Euler-Almansi, Log Euler-Almansi, Engineering and Biot. 7) Time Filters to filter out noisy data. Option should be provided to create separate Time Filtered Variable. For example, the user must have separate color plots of éxx and time filtered éxx. 8) Smooth of Data. 9) Indication of the appropriate subset size to be selected. 10) Computation of statistical data: mean, median, min., max., standard deviation... etc. 11) Export of plot and data to MATLAB. 12) Export of data to FEM Softwares. 13) Extrapolation of the data from the correlated displacement / strain data to the edge of the AOI. 14) Real time strain measutrement and option for the output signal to give feedback to the machine should be included 15) High temperature filters with spares and high temperature paints have to be supplied 16) A dedicated computer with state of the art configuration and latest version of the software must be included. 17) Vendor must to demonstrate strain measurements using the DIC system as well as strain gauge. These two measurements should be in agreement. Software licenses: 1. Portable USB License (Lifetime Validity) for – Image Acquisition Software + 3D Analysis + 2D Analysis Software must be provided. Installation and training at no extra cost The system should be installed and commissioned by the supplier at University of Hyderabad and give hands-on training and trial tests on the use of the system.

Part A: A Spinning Disk confocal ‘Inverted Fluorescent Microscope with Live Cell Capability Sl No Part A: Specification 1 Microscope: Fully Motorized Inverted Fluorescence Microscope for BF/Fluorescence with a dedicated remote touch panel/tab/controller and remote focus knob for controlling motorized components of the microscope. (Please provide necessary data on website / brochure) The plan Apochromatic objectives should have uniform field of view (FOV) throughout wide FOV of large Chip SCMOS (>21mm). Low Fluorescence Immersion Oil 100ml should be provided (minimum 5 bottles). 11 Stage top CO2 incubator setup for long-term live cell imaging including incubation system with Temperature, CO2 and humidity control. The parameters for incubation system should be controlled by software with the ability to record the temperature, CO2 levels at peridics intervals of atleast 10 minutes . Temp collar/Objective heater for High NA objectives should be provided. 12 SPINNING DISK CONFOCAL: Fully automated and motorized Microlens based dual Nipkow disk scanning unit: The Scan Head should have at least 2/dual disks with micro lens on both excitation and emission disk (SoRa disc equivalent). The super resolution should be a proven technology with optical theory with published documents on the technology be provided. The super resolution processing software should be real time and be based on structured illumination with selective high frequency pattern collection of demodulated emission signal in real time and and not by mere 3D deconvolution.
